No: 26-079                                                                                                                                September 29, 2026
CONTACT: Office of Public Affairs, 301-415-8200

          NRC Approves Construction of Nation’s First Small Modular Reactor
        TVA’s Clinch River Project Receives Construction Permit After 14-Month NRC Review

          ROCKVILLE, Md. — The Nuclear Regulatory Commission approved a construction
  permit for the Tennessee Valley Authority to build a small modular nuclear reactor at its Clinch
  River site in Oak Ridge, Tennessee, clearing the way for the nation’s first commercial small
  modular reactor and completing the NRC’s review in 14 months. This is the agency’s second
  major reactor approval this year.

         “Four months ahead of schedule is what the new NRC looks like,” NRC Chairman
  Ho K. Nieh said. “Today’s Clinch River decision demonstrates that the new NRC can make
  rigorous and credible safety decisions that enable major American nuclear projects to move
  forward.”

         The NRC formally began its review in July 2025 and completed its licensing decision in
  14 months, ahead of schedule. The approval follows a comprehensive safety evaluation
  completed by the NRC staff in June 2026, which found that TVA’s construction permit
  application met all regulatory requirements. The NRC also held a public hearing in Oak Ridge,
  Tennessee, in August as part of its modernized mandatory hearing process.

          TVA plans to build a 300-megawatt GE Vernova Hitachi boiling-water reactor to help
  meet growing regional power demand. Before loading fuel and starting operations, TVA will
  need a separate operating license from the NRC. TVA previously received an early site permit
  for the Clinch River site in 2019.

          More information on advanced reactor licensing is available at nrc.gov.




  The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission was created as an expert, technical agency to protect public
  health, safety, and security, and regulate the civilian use of nuclear materials, including enabling the
  deployment of nuclear power for the benefit of society. Among other responsibilities, the agency issues
  licenses, conducts inspections, initiates and enforces regulations, and plans for incident response. The NRC
  is collaborating with interagency partners to implement reforms outlined in new Executive Orders and the
  ADVANCE Act to streamline agency activities and enhance efficiency.
